source_text: Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα. Ἠρεμεῖν ἐβουλόμην, καὶ μὴ δημοσιεύειν ἀγροικίζουσαν γλῶσσαν· μέγα γὰρ σιωπή, ὅτ' ἂν ὁ λόγος εὐτελής· καὶ θαυμαστὸν ἡσυχία, ἀπαιδευσίας παρούσης· φιλόσοφός τε ἄκρος διὰ σιγῆς καλύπτων ἀμαθίαν. Τοῦτο κἀγὼ πράττειν προῃρούμην τὸ ἀσθενὲς τῆς οἰκείας ἐπιστάμενος γλώσσης· ἀλλ' ἕλκει με πρὸς τὸ λέγειν τῶν ὁρωμένων ἡ ὄψις. Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἡ πανήγυρις λαμπρὰ καὶ τὸ θέατρον συνεχές, καὶ ζέων ἐστὶ τῇ πίστει ὁ ἡμέτερος σύλλογος· ἐπὶ τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ λόγου θαρροῦντος τραπήσομαι· μάλιστα τοῦ Πατρὸς εὐχομένου, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας συναγωνιζομένης, μαρτύρων ἁγίων πρὸς τοῦτο ῥωννύντων τὸ ἀσθενές. Οὗτοι γὰρ καὶ γέροντας ἔπεισαν σὺν ἱδρῶτι πολλῷ μακρὰν ἐξανύσαι πορείαν, καὶ τὰ σφαλλόμενα βήματα τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τοῦ λόγου στηρίζειν κατηνάγκαζον· καὶ τὸ θῆλυ προέτρεψαν συνοδοιπορεῖν νεανίσκοις· καὶ τὴν νηπιάζουσαν ἡλικίαν ἕρπουσαν ἐνταῦθα παρήγαγον μάρτυρες κατὰ θανάτου σκιρτῶντες, ξίφεσιν ἐγγελῶντες, θυμὸν τυραννικὸν διαρπάζοντες, θάνατον ἀθανασίας πρόξενον ἀνθαρπάζοντες, ἐν ἰδίῳ πτώματι τὴν νίκην οἰκειούμενοι, διὰ σώματος ἀναπηδῶντες πρὸς οὐρανόν. Τὰ μέλη διασκορπίζοντες ἵνα σφίγξωσι τὰς ψυχάς, τὰ κλεῖθρα τῆς ζωῆς διαρρήξαντες ἵνα τὰς κλεῖς ἀνοίξωσι τῶν οὐρανῶν. Ὁ ἀπιστῶν ὅτι θάνατος καταλέλυται, ᾅδης πεπάτηται, ὅτι τούτου τὰ δεσμὰ διεράγη· ὅτι τύραννος δέδεται· βλεπέτω μάρτυρας κυβιστῶντας κατὰ θανάτου, καὶ τὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ νίκην ἀνευφημοῦντας. Ὢ τοῦ θαύματος. Ἀφ' οὗπερ Χριστὸς τὸν ᾅδην ἐσκύλευσεν, ἄνθρωποι κατωρχήσαντο τοῦ θανάτου. Ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον; ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος; Ἐσκύλευται ὁ ᾅδης καὶ ὁ διάβολος· καὶ τῆς ἀρχαίας ἀφῄρηται πανοπλίας· καὶ τοῦ οἰκείου κράτους ἐκβέβληται.
thought_title: The martyrs' festival compels speech and displays victory over death
orientation: The preacher opens the sermon by explaining why he speaks despite his unpolished tongue, then describes how the holy martyrs draw all ages to the festival and leap against death.
pass_a_gloss: Bless, Master. I was wishing to be still, and not to publish a tongue speaking rustically; for silence is great, whenever the word is cheap; and stillness is wonderful, when lack of learning is present; and a man is a top philosopher by covering ignorance through silence. This I too was choosing to do, knowing the weakness of my own tongue; but the sight of the things being seen drags me toward speaking. Since therefore the festival is bright and the theater is packed, and our assembly is boiling in faith; I will turn to the beginning of the speech with confidence; especially since the Father is praying, the Church is fighting alongside, the holy martyrs are strengthening the weakness toward this. For these both persuaded old men to complete a long journey with much sweat, and they were forcing the faltering steps to be supported by the staff of the word; and they urged the female to travel together with young men; and the martyrs led the infant age crawling here, leaping against death, laughing at swords, plundering tyrannical rage, seizing death as the agent of immortality, making the victory their own in their own fall, leaping up through the body toward heaven. Scattering the limbs in order that they may bind the souls, having broken the bars of life in order that they may open the keys of the heavens. The one who disbelieves that death has been destroyed, that Hades has been trampled, that its bonds have been burst; that the tyrant has been bound; let him look at the martyrs tumbling against death, and acclaiming the victory of Christ. O the wonder. From the time when Christ plundered Hades, humans have danced down upon death. Where, O death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, is your victory? Hades has been plundered and the devil; and he has been stripped of the ancient armor; and he has been cast out from his own dominion.

choices.why: Keeps the participle's active force and the rural, unpolished connotation of ἀγροικίζω without importing a modern idiom.
εὐτελής means of little worth; 'cheap' preserves the evaluative force and the generalizing ἂν clause.
rejected: when the word is of no value

choices.why: συνεχές here means continuous, crowded, unbroken; 'packed' renders the spatial sense of a full assembly.

choices.term: ζέων ἐστὶ τῇ πίστει ὁ ἡμέτερος σύλλογος
choices.english: our assembly is boiling in faith
choices.why: ζέων is a strong heat metaphor; 'boiling' keeps the intensity and the dative of sphere.
rejected: our assembly is fervent in faith
our gathering is zealous in faith

choices.english: seizing death as the agent of immortality
choices.why: πρόξενος is a patron or agent who procures something; 'agent of immortality' preserves the paradox that death procures immortality.
rejected: snatching death as the procurer of immortality
seizing death as the sponsor of immortality

choices.why: κατορχέομαι takes a genitive and means to dance over or against someone in triumph; 'danced down upon' keeps the directional and mocking force.

bible_refs.note: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον; ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος;

pass_b_english: Bless, Master. I wanted to remain silent and not publish a tongue speaking rustically, for silence is a great thing whenever the word is cheap, and stillness is admirable when lack of learning is present; and the highest philosopher is one who hides ignorance through silence. This is what I too chose to do, knowing the weakness of my own tongue. But the sight of what I see drags me toward speaking. Since, then, the festival is splendid and the theater is packed, and our assembly is boiling in faith, I will turn to the beginning of my speech with confidence—especially since the Father prays, the Church strives alongside, and the holy martyrs strengthen my weakness for this task.

For these martyrs persuaded old men to complete a long journey with much sweat, and they compelled them to steady their faltering steps by the staff of the word. They urged the female sex to travel together with young men, and they led the infant age crawling here. The martyrs leap against death, laugh at swords, plunder the tyrant's rage, seize death as the agent of immortality, make victory their own in their very fall, and leap through their bodies toward heaven. They scatter their limbs in order to bind their souls; they break the bars of life in order to open the keys of heaven.

Let the one who disbelieves that death has been destroyed, that Hades has been trampled, that its bonds have been torn apart, that the tyrant has been bound—let that one look at the martyrs tumbling against death and acclaiming the victory of Christ. O the wonder! From the time Christ plundered Hades, human beings have triumphed over death. Where, O death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, is your victory? (Hosea 13:14 / 1 Corinthians 15:55). Hades has been plundered, and the devil too; he has been stripped of his ancient armor, and he has been cast out from his own dominion.

problems.why: κατωρχήσαντο means 'triumphed over'/'mocked' death, not 'danced down upon'
problems.fix: human beings have triumphed over death
problems.ruling: κατωρχήσαντο means 'triumphed over/mocked,' not 'danced down upon'; mistranslates the verb's sense.

edits.old: human beings have danced down upon death
edits.new: human beings have triumphed over death

fixed: Corrected 'danced down upon death' to 'triumphed over death': κατωρχήσαντο means 'triumphed over'/'mocked', not 'danced down upon'.

problems.quote: they compelled their faltering steps to be steadied
problems.source_quote: τὰ σφαλλόμενα βήματα τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τοῦ λόγου στηρίζειν κατηνάγκαζον
problems.why: Middle/passive confusion: martyrs compelled old men to steady their own steps, not 'were compelled'.
problems.fix: they compelled them to steady their faltering steps with the staff of the word
problems.ruling: στηρίζειν is active: 'to steady faltering steps', not 'to be steadied'; passive voice misrepresents the action.

problems.source_quote: Ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον; ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος;
problems.why: Citation alone as 1 Cor 15:55; source follows LXX Hosea 13:14 form with νῖκος not νίκη.
problems.ruling: Source uses νῖκος (Hosea 13:14 LXX form), not νίκη; citing only 1 Cor 15:55 misleads readers on textual source.

edits.old: they compelled their faltering steps to be steadied
edits.new: they compelled them to steady their faltering steps

fixed: Source: 'τὰ σφαλλόμενα βήματα τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τοῦ λόγου στηρίζειν κατηνάγκαζον' — the martyrs compelled the old men to steady their own faltering steps; the English 'they compelled their faltering steps to be steadied' misreads the middle/passive. Fixed to 'they compelled them to steady their faltering steps'.

Source: 'Ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον; ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος;' — the form follows the Septuagint of Hosea 13:14 with νῖκος, so the citation should include Hosea 13:14 alongside 1 Corinthians 15:55. Fixed.

last_rejected.quote: Where, O death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, is your victory? (Hosea 13:14 / 1 Corinthians 15:55)
last_rejected.source_quote: Ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον; ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος;
last_rejected.why: Source marks this as a rhetorical taunt, not authorial speech; English hides quoted voice.
last_rejected.fix: Introduce as taunt: 'So we cry: Where, O death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, your victory?'
last_rejected.ruling: Parenthetical scripture reference is standard; no speaker voice in source. Mere preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: κυβιστῶντας means somersaulting/leaping acrobatically, not 'tumbling' as falling; loses athletic triumph.
last_rejected.fix: somersaulting against death, or leaping in triumph over death
last_rejected.ruling: κυβιστῶντας = tumbling/somersaulting; 'tumbling' is within normal range. Mere preference.

last_rejected.why: ἀνευφημοῦντας means 'hailing with loud cries of triumph,' not merely 'acclaiming'; weakens force.
last_rejected.fix: hailing Christ's victory with loud triumph
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνευφημοῦντας = acclaiming/shouting triumph; 'acclaiming' is within normal range. Mere preference.

last_rejected.why: ἐβουλόμην is imperfect 'I was wishing/wanting,' not simple past; ongoing resolve, not completed decision.
last_rejected.fix: I was wishing to remain silent
last_rejected.ruling: ἐβουλόμην imperfect often renders as simple past 'I wanted'; normal range. Mere preference.
